name: Malta
description:
A Mediterranean microstate with a thriving economy and excellent location. Malta offers EU membership, English-speaking communities, sunny weather, and growing opportunities in gaming and iGaming sectors.

## Key Highlights
- EU membership with English-speaking locals
- Year-round sunny weather and Mediterranean living
- Growing iGaming and fintech industries
longdescription: Malta is a small Mediterranean island nation and EU member state strategically located between Europe and North Africa. Valletta, the capital, is a UNESCO World Heritage city with stunning architecture and harbor views. English is an official language alongside Maltese, making it highly accessible to English speakers. Malta enjoys Mediterranean climate with sunny weather year-round, attracting retirees and those seeking consistent sunshine. The economy is small but vibrant, with gaming, iGaming, and online gambling being significant industries. Financial services and tourism are also important sectors. Malta actively attracts tech entrepreneurs and remote workers. EU citizenship can be obtained through investment programs. The cost of living is moderate. Healthcare is good and publicly funded. Malta's size (about 500,000 people) makes it intimate and easy to navigate. The country has low crime rates and is very safe. Malta offers incredible beaches and Mediterranean beauty. The iGaming and fintech sectors are thriving. Challenges include summer heat and tourist crowds, visa restrictions for non-EU citizens, and limited job market outside specific sectors. Malta combines Mediterranean charm, EU membership, English-language accessibility, safety, year-round sunshine, growing tech opportunities, and citizenship investment options, making it attractive for entrepreneurs, remote workers, retirees, and EU passport seekers.

visas.name: Nomad Residence Permit (Malta)
visas.description: Nomad Residence Permit for remote workers who want to live and work from Malta's Mediterranean shores.

visas.name: Malta Student Visa
visas.description: Malta's student visa for non-EU/EEA nationals enrolled in a full-time recognised study programme in Malta for more than 90 days, with the right to work part-time during studies.

visas.name: Malta Family Reunification Permit
visas.description: Malta's family reunification permit allows non-EU spouses and minor dependent children of non-EU residents legally living in Malta to join them in Malta for long-term residence.

visas.name: Malta Self-Employment Permit
visas.description: Malta's self-employment permit allows non-EU nationals to establish and run their own business in Malta, an English-speaking EU member with a business-friendly regulatory environment.
benefits: Run your own business in Malta

visas.name: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP)
visas.description: Malta's Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP) grants non-EU investors permanent residency through a qualifying property purchase/rental and government contribution, offering Schengen Area access.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Children of Maltese parent(s) acquire Maltese citizenship automatically. EU citizenship through descent available.

Naturalization.desc:
**Requirements:** 5 years legal residence, Maltese or English language, good conduct, financial independence.

**Processing:** Through Ministry for Justice, 6-12 months.

Investment Citizenship.desc: Individual Investor Programme (IIP) offers citizenship through property investment €320,000, government contribution €88,000, and donation €10,000.

Birthright Citizenship.desc: Children born in Malta to resident parents may acquire citizenship upon registration.

tax_advice:
- Malta has a favorable tax treaty network with 70+ countries
- Corporate tax rate is 35%, but can be reduced with tax credits
- Individuals receive a personal allowance of €8,500 annually
- VAT rate is 18% (reduced rates of 5% and 0% apply to certain goods/services)
- Non-resident individuals only taxed on Malta-sourced income
- Capital gains are generally not taxable in Malta
- Dividend withholding tax is 6/7 (effectively 0% for domestic dividends)
- Foreign tax credits available for taxes paid abroad
local_tips:
- Learn basic Maltese and English are both official languages
- Apply for residency before 60 days if staying longer than 90 days
- Healthcare: Private insurance recommended; public system available for residents
- Cost of living highest in EU capitals; budget €1,500-2,000/month for comfortable living
- Buy property early if considering Golden Visa; prices rising quickly
- Network through local expat groups; tight community makes integration easier
- Public transport is cheap but limited; car recommended outside Valletta
